title: Smooth curves decompose into connected curves and rational points
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension at most one (a smooth curve of [def-sc-curves]). There are a finite set $I$, smooth separated connected one-dimensional finite-type $k$-schemes $D_i$ for $i\in I$, and a finite set $J$, with an isomorphism of $k$-schemes $C\cong(\coprod_{i\in I}D_i)\amalg(\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Spec}k)$. The coprojections are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and each index set may be empty. Coproducts are those of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

proof.text: The field k is Noetherian (its only ideals are 0 and k), and Spec k is a one-point quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to C \to Spec k to obtain that C is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] its irreducible components form a finite family.

By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], the irreducible components cover C. Form the finite graph whose vertices are the irreducible components and whose edges join intersecting components. For each graph component a let U_a be the union of its vertices. These unions are disjoint, cover C, and are closed as finite unions of closed sets; each is open because its complement is the union of the other U_b. An irreducible space is connected: a separation into two nonempty clopen sets contradicts its definition. Along an edge the union of two connected sets meeting at a point is connected, since a separation would put both sets in the same part; induction along graph paths makes U_a connected. Thus the U_a are precisely the nonempty connected components of C, and there are finitely many; when C is empty there are none.

source.place: lemma-irreducible and lemma-Noetherian: finite-component topological argument

proof.text: Give U_a its open-subscheme structure C_a. Its inclusion is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion]. It is also a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]: its image is closed, and on stalks the map to the pushforward is the identity at points in U_a and has zero target outside U_a, whose complement is open. Smoothness of C_a over k is [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a), with V = Spec k. Smoothness includes local finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], whose finite polynomial presentations in particular give locally finite type. C_a is quasi-compact as a closed subset of the quasi-compact C, so it is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its diagonal is the pullback of the closed immersion diagonal of C along C_a times_k C_a \to C times_k C; [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change] makes this a closed immersion, proving separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

By [def-sc-curves], C is a smooth curve, so [lem-sc-smooth-regular] gives regular local rings at every point. The stalks of C_a equal the corresponding stalks of C, and C_a is locally Noetherian as an open subscheme of the Noetherian C. Hence C_a is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. It is nonempty and connected by step 2, so [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] gives integrality. Since U_a is closed in C, every chain of irreducible closed subsets of U_a is also such a chain in C; by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] its dimension is at most one. Nonemptiness gives a chain of length zero, so its dimension is either zero or one.

Partition the finite component indices into I of dimension one and J of dimension zero. For i in I set D_i = C_i; step 3 and [def-sc-curves] give exactly the asserted connected smooth curves. For j in J apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dim-integral-point] to the integral finite-type k-scheme C_j of dimension zero from steps 3-4: its structure morphism identifies it with Spec k as a k-scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] form the coproduct of all C_a. The inclusions give a morphism from that coproduct to C; its inverse on each disjoint open U_a is the inverse of the identification with C_a followed by its coprojection. These local inverses glue because the U_a have empty pairwise intersections, and both composites restrict to identities on the covering opens. Thus this is an isomorphism over k. Replace the J summands by their structure isomorphisms and reorder the finite family into I and J; the resulting coprojections are the component inclusions from step 3. The empty C gives the empty coproduct.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_curve_points_decomposition (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [Smooth f] : ∃ (I J : Type u) (_ : Fintype I) (_ : Fintype J) (D : I → Scheme.{u}) (d : ∀ i, D i ⟶ Spec (.of k)), (∀ i, IsConnectedCurve (d i)) ∧ (∀ i, Smooth (d i)) ∧ ∃ (q : (∐ fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) ⟶ Spec (.of k)), (∀ i, Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) (Sum.inl i) ≫ q = d i) ∧ (∀ j, Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) (Sum.inr j) ≫ q = 𝟙 _) ∧ ∃ (e : C ≅ ∐ fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)), e.hom ≫ q = f ∧ (∀ s, IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) s)) ∧ (∀ s, IsClosedImmersion (Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) s))
